==English==
{{wikidata lexeme|L5626}}

===Alternative forms===
* {{alt|en|acheivement||misspelling}}

===Etymology===
{{etymon|en|:bor|frm:achevement<ety:inh<fro:achevement>>|tree=1}}
From {{bor|en|frm|achevement}} (compare Modern {{cog|fr|achèvement}}), from {{der|en|fro|achevement}}, from the verb {{m|fro|achever}}, {{m|fro|achiever|t=to finish}}; equivalent to {{suffix|en|achieve|ment}}. The heraldic sense may be influenced by {{m|en|hatchment}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/əˈt͡ʃiːv.mənt/|[əˈt͡ʃʰiːv.mɪ̈nt̚]}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-achievement.ogg|a=US}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun|~}}

# The act of [[achieving]] or performing; a [[successful]] performance; [[accomplishment]].
#* {{RQ:Allingham China Governess|chapter=1|passage=The original family who had begun to build a palace to rival Nonesuch had died out before they had put up little more than the gateway, so that the actual structure which had come down to posterity retained the secret magic of a promise rather than the overpowering splendour of a great architectural '''achievement'''.}}
#* {{quote-journal
|en
|year=2012
|month=March-April
|author=[[w:Terry Sejnowski|Terrence J. Sejnowski]]
|title=Well-connected Brains
|volume=100
|issue=2
|page=171
|magazine=w:American Scientist
|url=http://www.americanscientist.org/bookshelf/pub/well-connected-brains
|passage=Creating a complete map of the human connectome would therefore be a monumental milestone but not the end of the journey to understanding how our brains work. The '''achievement''' will transform neuroscience and serve as the starting point for asking questions we could not otherwise have answered, […].
|accessdate=24 May 2013
|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170427064626/http://www.americanscientist.org/bookshelf/pub/well-connected-brains
|archivedate=27 April 2017
}}
# A [[great]] or [[heroic]] [[deed]] or [[feat]]; something accomplished by [[valor]] or [[boldness]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=c. 1837|author=w:Thomas Babington Macaulay|title=Minutes on the Education of India|passage={{...}}the English genius was effecting in science a revolution which will, to the end of time, be reckoned among the highest '''achievements''' of the human intellect.}}
# {{lb|en|heraldry}} An [[escutcheon]] or [[ensign]] [[armorial]]; a full display or depiction of all the heraldic components to which the bearer of a [[coat of arms]] is entitled; {{lb|en|now|especially}} a funeral shield: the [[hatchment]].
#: {{mero|en|shield|supporter|crest|motto}} <!-- Reference: Wikipedia: Coat of arms -->
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1791|author={{w|Charlotte Smith (writer)|Charlotte Smith}}|title=Celestina|publisher=Broadview|year_published=2004|page=488
|passage=The narrow Gothic windows were filled, not with glass that admitted the light, but with glass painted with the '''achievements''' of the family {{...}}.}}
# {{lb|en|video games}} An award for completing a particular task or meeting an objective in a [[video game]].
#: {{synonyms|en|trophy|chiev}}
#: {{ux|en|Finishing the game does not give you a 100% score until you have unlocked all of the '''achievements'''.}}
# {{sid|en|aspect}} {{lb|en|grammar|semantics}} The [[lexical aspect]] ([[aktionsart]]) of [[verb]]s or [[predicate]]s that change in an instant.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1997|author=Robert van Valin; Randy LaPolla|title=Syntax|page=92|text={{...}}distinctions among states of affairs are reflected to a striking degree in distinctions among ''Aktionsart'' types. That is, situations are expressed by state verbs or predicates, events by '''achievement''' verbs or predicates, and actions by activity verbs or predicates.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=DxcrbgT1_oMC&pg=PA92}}
# {{lb|en|sociology}} The successful completion of a socially defined goal or task, highlighting individual or group accomplishment.
